findings.body: Cancellation runs only through processLiveAdmissionWorkItem. Startup and periodic recovery instead enqueue the group directly (message-loop.ts:336–349; live-execution.ts:565,580). If recovery handles /stop while earlier messages are still deferred, excludeWaiting skips those messages and takes the command alone. The normal stop handler (session-commands.ts:287–293) does not consume the waiting batch. The admission worker subsequently sees the command already consumed and returns before this cancellation block, so the supposedly cancelled messages can still start a turn. Apply cancellation through the normal command path as well.
findings.title: Not done: /stop cancels a waiting batch as history

findings.body: This heuristic does not recognize every command accepted by the runtime parser. For a route whose trigger is Andy, `Andy /stop` is a valid command because extractSessionCommand removes the configured trigger (session-command-parse.ts:184–198), but this regex assigns it a 1.5-second window. The parser also accepts whitespace after a mention-friendly bang, such as `@Andy ! stop`, which this regex misses. Determine command status using the same normalization and route trigger as the runtime parser so valid session commands consistently bypass the window.
findings.title: Not done: session commands never wait

findings.body: The burst test claims items using a clock advanced by ten seconds and invokes processGroupMessages directly. It therefore bypasses the admission scheduler that must start the batch at the promised time. The stop test likewise supplies a replacement command handler that always succeeds (lines 309–312). The changed end-to-end test explicitly expires the window before enqueueing work, so it does not supply the missing proof. Add an owner end-to-end scenario through the real admission and command paths, with Postgres and fake channel/runner edges, asserting one reply after the window and cancellation without a later reply.
findings.title: Not done: end-to-end proof of quiet-window behavior

findings.body: consumeAll filters only by scope and unconsumed status (live-admission-work-item-repository.postgres.ts:335–355). If another message or session command is saved after /stop but before this call executes, it is also marked stopped and never processed. For example, `/stop` followed immediately by `/status` can silently discard the status command. Bound cancellation by the stop item's receive order so later requests remain eligible.
findings.title: Limit /stop cancellation to messages preceding the command
